findings.title: Google credential key stored as zod SafeParse wrapper object
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)`, i.e. `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, not the parsed key. The previous code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returned the key itself. The result is now written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the stored credential becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` and will fail `googleCredentialSchema.parse` on the next use, breaking every Google Calendar connection after a token refresh.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported in salesforce CalendarService
findings.body: `prisma.credential.update(...)` is called in `getClient`, but there is no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` in this file. This is a compile/runtime error (ReferenceError at request time), breaking every Salesforce calendar operation.

findings.title: Credential-sync path returns a fetch Response where callers expect axios/SDK shapes
findings.body: When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` always returns a `fetch` Response. Callers such as zoho-bigin, zohocrm (`tokenInfo.data.*`) and hubspot (expects a `HubspotToken` object with `expiresIn`/`accessToken`) read properties that do not exist on a `Response`. With syncing enabled those apps will throw or silently write `undefined` keys to the credential. The sync response must be normalized per-caller or parsed as JSON.

findings.title: credentialId passed where userId is expected to the credential sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id as the `userId` argument. The helper sends it as `calcomUserId` to the self-hosted sync endpoint, so the wrong user's credentials would be fetched/refreshed. `credential.userId` should be threaded through `refreshAccessToken` instead.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys are meaningless and strip required fields
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the same stringified object key (e.g. "[object Object]"), so the schema does not "assume any numeric property is the expiry" nor allow arbitrary extra properties. Because zod strips unknown keys by default, the parsed `data` when credential sharing is enabled contains only `access_token`, dropping `refresh_token`, `expiry_date`/`expires_in` and provider-specific fields. Callers then persist an incomplete credential key, breaking subsequent refreshes.

findings.title: Fake literal "refresh_token" injected into credential keys
findings.body: If the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the code assigns the literal string `"refresh_token"`. Callers store this value in the DB credential, so a real missing/omitted refresh token is replaced by a bogus value instead of preserving the existing one. Future refresh attempts will send `refresh_token=refresh_token` and fail with invalid_grant, requiring users to reconnect.

findings.title: Unvalidated input paths throw unhandled errors (500) and no HTTP method check
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` can throw, producing an unhandled rejection / opaque 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message. The handler also accepts any HTTP method (GET included), so credentials could be mutated via a GET with a query-shaped body. Use `safeParse`/try-catch and restrict to POST.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality and no length guard
findings.body: The shared secret is compared with `!==` against a header value, which is vulnerable to timing analysis, and `req.headers[name]` may be an array if the header is repeated (comparison then always fails/succeeds unpredictably). Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on normalized string values.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes token on every client creation and then ignores the new token
findings.body: `getClient` unconditionally POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint on every service instantiation (no expiry check), which wastes a request and risks rate limiting. Worse, the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still built with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` / `instance_url` rather than `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`, so the refresh has no effect on the connection. It also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce is excluded from the credential-sync feature this PR adds.

findings.title: Fragile `response.statusText !== "OK"` success check
findings.body: `statusText` is not guaranteed to be "OK" (it is empty on HTTP/2 and varies across runtimes/proxies), so successful refreshes can be rejected with a 400 HttpError. Check `response.ok` / `response.status` instead.

findings.title: App slug "zoomvideo" does not match the Zoom app slug used elsewhere
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", ...)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the sync endpoint, but the app's slug in the DB/app store (and the value the new `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint looks up) is `zoom`. A self-hoster implementing the sync endpoint will receive an unknown slug and cannot map it back, breaking Zoom credential syncing.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean
findings.body: The expression returns `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (string) or `undefined`/empty string rather than a boolean. It is consumed in boolean contexts and typed as such by consumers; wrap with `!!(...)` to avoid leaking the encryption key value into a client-importable constant module and to keep the type honest.
